A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same vesselFM study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching supplementary content across reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments on four datasets, architectural and data-source ablations, and synthetic-image comparisons in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds specialist-model comparisons, statistical analyses and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The three-source framework, domain-randomization generator, mask/class conditioning, flow-matching objective and segmentation losses are retained. The DynUNet configuration is newly specified, without establishing an architecture change; preprocessing and training-setting revisions are assessed under E3.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 17 annotated sources organized into 23 datasets and evaluate OCTA, BvEM, SMILE-UHURA and MSD8 under zero-, one- and few-shot settings. The specialist comparisons introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 7 substantially extends comparison coverage with specialists trained separately on TopCoW, VesSAP and CSD, evaluated across all four datasets and three shot settings. Table 2 retains its comparators. Figure 11 also extends the qualitative comparison with Med-DDPM examples.

E3.justification: The documented experimental recipe changes across preprocessing and training: SMILE-UHURA/MSD8 resampling is removed, Gaussian smoothing replaces median label filtering, and Algorithm 1 uses a 3×3×3 rather than 5×5×5 closing element. Training decay ends at 10^-5 rather than 10^-6, rotation narrows from 0–45 to 0–10 degrees, and fine-tuning noise changes. Table 1 also revises sample counts. These are reported setting changes; rerunning experiments is not established.

E4.justification: Figure 11 expands the qualitative examination of synthetic-image fidelity, particularly through additional Med-DDPM examples. The existing data-source, generator, architecture and data-scaling ablations in Tables 3–6 and Figure 9 are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides no formal significance analysis. New Appendix K introduces paired t-tests against runner-up configurations across the main quantitative comparisons, including exact p-values and a nonsignificant class-conditioning Dice result. Repeated-run counts, seeds and the pairing units remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 retain their scores, while Table 7 adds substantial specialist-comparison results: for example, few-shot SMILE-UHURA Dice is 78.20 for the CSD specialist versus 78.77 for vesselFM. Appendices K–L add significance findings and computational measurements, including 30.6 ms inference on an A100 for a 128³ volume. Table 1 revises reported dataset statistics.

T1.justification: The flow-matching ODE, conditional objective, interpolation path and Euler sampling derivation in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same universal vessel-segmentation claims, three-source approach and zero-/one-/few-shot superiority claims. The shortened conclusion and additional appendix evidence do not substantively redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix D explains the from-scratch model's performance through imaging-domain differences, architectural biases and representation mismatch. Appendix F describes clinical annotation bootstrapping through pre-segmentation and iterative refinement. The conclusion also revises future directions to include instance segmentation.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies DynUNet strides, kernels, filters and residual blocks. Appendix L adds parameter count, device-specific inference times and memory consumption. Preprocessing and training instructions are revised, although the exact 90,685-patch training count and some earlier setting details disappear. The code-access link is retained.

R1.justification: The same 62 referenced works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Bibliographic corrections and expanded discussion of already cited baselines do not establish a revised novelty claim or research positioning.

P1.justification: The main text receives localized language edits and a shorter conclusion. The appendix is lettered and reorganized, including moving experimental details ahead of the extended ablation discussion and adding dedicated explanatory sections. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7 and expands/rearranges Figure 11 with a Med-DDPM panel. Supplementary material and acknowledgments shift position, and some captions change. The other fifteen image figures are identical, and existing result-table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The precise architecture specification, specialist comparisons and computational measurements improve reproducibility and practical assessment. Statistical testing also qualifies the small class-conditioning benefit. These gains are limited by unspecified t-test pairing/sample details and unexplained setting revisions alongside unchanged existing scores; they support a modest overall improvement.
